name: David J. Crandall
title: Luddy Professor of Computer Science; Department Chair; Director of the Luddy AI Center
department: Computer Science; IU Computer Vision Lab; Luddy Artificial Intelligence Center
fitReason: Strong CS-method overlap through visual perception, real-time multimodal behavior analysis and LLM dialogue on an embodied social robot. A nonclinical perception, dialogue-system or software evaluation project is plausible, conditional on a defined eight-week project and host approval.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full 2024 primary study implements autonomous scripted-plus-LLM conversation on a LuxAI QTrobot with moving head and arms, evaluated with 19 older adults in an IU lab and two care facilities. Crandall is an IU coauthor. The official 2026 HRI program lists the IRIS demo with Crandall, and a demo coauthor explicitly identifies the QT platform and AI-generated follow-ups. The 2026 BehaviorKit paper adds robot-facing multimodal perception software; its example clip evaluation is not itself a new physical robot trial. Exact inspected hardware-study methods date to 2024, so physical evidence is conservatively capped at 20.

shortVisit.summary: The full official lab alumni roster records an external MS student from Sungkyunkwan University who visited as a research intern in summer 2024, plus a WUSTL visiting MS student in summer 2019. These establish historical master's visitor precedents, not a current invitation or summer 2027 vacancy. No explicit live short-visit intake was found on the inspected faculty and lab pages.

scoreReasons.fit: strong perception/multimodal/LLM methods plus physical HRI.
scoreReasons.physical: direct QTrobot study, conservatively capped because fully inspected experimental methods are from 2024 and collaborative.
scoreReasons.freshness: dated 2026 BehaviorKit paper and HRI demo. Provisional evidence-fit score, not acceptance probability or prestige.
